channel.title: PoolChem Tracker Blog
channel.description: Pool chemistry guides, tips, and maintenance advice from PoolChem Tracker.

item.title: Pool Closing Chemicals Checklist: What to Buy and How Much
item.description: Complete list of chemicals you need to close a pool for winter — what each one does, how much to buy, and the order to add them. Covers in-ground and above-ground pools.

item.title: How Much Stabilizer to Add to a Pool (Dose Chart by Pool Size)
item.description: About 13 oz per 10,000 gallons raises CYA by 10 ppm. Full dose chart by pool size for common target increases, the exact formula, step-by-step addition process, and why you should never add stabilizer to the skimmer basket.

item.title: Low CYA in a Pool: Signs, Risks, and How to Fix It
item.description: Low CYA leaves chlorine unprotected from UV — a pool with CYA near zero can lose most of its FC in a few hours of direct sunlight. How to recognize it, why it happens, and how a single dose of granular stabilizer fixes it.

item.title: Best CYA Level for Liquid Chlorine Pools: 30–50 ppm Explained
item.description: Target 30–50 ppm CYA for a liquid chlorine pool. Below 30 ppm UV destroys chlorine too fast; above 60–70 ppm the required FC minimum becomes hard to maintain. Liquid chlorine adds zero CYA, so once you're in range it stays stable.

item.title: High CYA in a Pool: Symptoms, Why It Happens, and How to Fix It
item.description: High CYA makes chlorine progressively less effective — most summer algae in pools that "have chlorine" traces back to CYA above 80 ppm. Signs it's too high, how it got there (trichlor tablets), and the only fix: partial drain and refill.

item.title: How to Raise CYA in a Pool: Add Stabilizer the Right Way
item.description: Add granular cyanuric acid (stabilizer) to raise CYA — about 13 oz per 10,000 gallons raises CYA by 10 ppm. How to add it correctly, how long to wait before retesting, what target to aim for, and when to use trichlor tablets instead.

item.title: How to Lower CYA in a Pool: Drain and Refill, Step by Step
item.description: The only way to lower CYA is to drain part of the pool and refill with fresh water. Here's how to calculate exactly how much to drain, what to rebalance after, and how to keep CYA from climbing again.

item.title: What Is CYA (Pool Stabilizer)? Ideal Levels and How to Manage It
item.description: Pool stabilizer and CYA are the same chemical — cyanuric acid. Ideal range: 30–50 ppm for regular pools, 60–80 ppm for saltwater. How it works, how it builds up, and what to do when it's off.

item.title: How to Close a Pool for Winter: Step-by-Step Checklist
item.description: Step-by-step pool closing checklist: when to winterize, chemistry targets, blowing out lines, equipment draining, and the right chemical order. Close right in fall, open clear in spring.

item.title: Pool Cloudy After Adding Chemicals? Here's What Happened
item.description: Brief cloudiness after adding CYA, calcium chloride, or soda ash is normal and clears in under 2 hours. Cloudiness lasting past 24 hours means pH or calcium is out of balance. Chemical-by-chemical breakdown.

item.title: Pool Cloudy but Chemistry Is Fine? It's Your Filter
item.description: When pool water stays cloudy despite correct chemistry, the cause is almost always filtration — not enough run time, dirty media, or worn-out sand. Here's how to diagnose and fix each type.

item.title: Pool Cloudy After Rain? Here's the Fix
item.description: Rain dilutes free chlorine, washes in algae spores and phosphates, and raises water level — all of which cause cloudy water within 24–48 hours. Test FC first; here's what to do next.

item.title: Why Algae Keeps Coming Back in Your Pool (And How to Stop It)
item.description: Recurring pool algae has a root cause that wasn't fixed. The five most common reasons: FC below your CYA minimum, high CYA, incomplete treatment, contaminated equipment, and dead spots. Track your readings to find the pattern.

item.title: Black Algae in a Pool: What It Is and How to Get Rid of It
item.description: Black algae (cyanobacteria) forms a hard shell on plaster and roots into pool surfaces — regular shocking doesn't work. Here's the wire-brush and sustained shock treatment that actually eliminates it.

item.title: Mustard Algae vs. Green Algae: How to Tell Them Apart and Treat Each
item.description: Mustard algae is yellow-brown slime that brushes off easily but keeps coming back. Green algae clouds the whole pool. They need different treatments — and mustard algae won't clear without decontaminating swimsuits and gear.

item.title: How to Kill Pool Algae: Step-by-Step Guide
item.description: Kill pool algae by raising FC to shock level (CYA × 40%), brushing surfaces daily, and holding FC until the overnight chlorine loss test passes. Complete guide for green, mustard, and black algae.

item.title: Pool Calcium Hardness Too High? How to Lower It
item.description: The only way to lower calcium hardness is a partial drain and refill — no chemical treatment removes dissolved calcium. Learn the dilution formula to calculate exactly how much water to swap out.

item.title: Pool Alkalinity Too Low? How to Raise It With Baking Soda
item.description: Low pool alkalinity causes pH to bounce wildly and makes water corrosive. Baking soda is the fix — here's how much to add, what to expect, and how to keep TA stable long-term.

item.title: Pool pH Too Low? How to Raise It (Soda Ash vs Baking Soda)
item.description: pH below 7.2 means corrosive water. Learn how to raise it and whether to use soda ash or baking soda — the answer depends on your alkalinity reading.

item.title: Pool Chlorine Too High — What to Do
item.description: High FC after shocking? How to lower pool chlorine safely — sunlight, dilution, and when to use a neutralizer — plus what "too high" actually means for your CYA level.

item.title: Chlorine Lock: Myth or Real?
item.description: Chlorine lock is a myth. If chlorine isn't working in your pool, the real cause is high CYA, active organic demand, or both — here's how to diagnose and fix it.

item.title: Why Does My Pool Smell Like Chlorine?
item.description: A strong chlorine smell means too little chlorine, not too much. Combined chlorine (chloramines) causes the odor — here's what it is, why it forms, and how to fix it.

item.title: How Long After Shocking Can You Swim?
item.description: Wait until FC drops to your normal target range — not a fixed number of hours. How to test before you swim, and what safe FC looks like at different CYA levels.

item.title: How to Shock a Pool: Step-by-Step Guide
item.description: Shock your pool by raising FC to CYA × 40%. Step-by-step process for clearing algae, destroying chloramines, and knowing when you're done.

item.title: Pool Chlorine Guide Index
item.description: All chlorine guides in one place — FC/CYA ratio, raising and holding chlorine, liquid vs tablets, combined chlorine causes and fixes.

item.title: Pool pH Guide Index
item.description: All pH guides in one place — ideal pH targets, how to raise and lower pH, diagnosing persistent pH rise.

item.title: Pool Alkalinity Guide Index
item.description: All alkalinity guides in one place — TA targets, muriatic acid method, baking soda vs soda ash, the alkalinity-pH relationship.

item.title: Pool Calcium Guide Index
item.description: All calcium guides in one place — hardness targets by surface type, scale, corrosion, white flakes, and salt cell deposits.

item.title: Cloudy Pool Water Guide Index
item.description: All cloudy water guides in one place — diagnosing and clearing hazy pool water, post-shock cloudiness, dead algae, high-alkalinity haze.

item.title: LSI Guide Index
item.description: All LSI guides in one place — Langelier Saturation Index formula, calculator differences, surface implications, saltwater and rain effects.

item.title: Pool Testing Guide Index
item.description: All pool testing guides in one place — test kit types, test frequency, sampling technique, and what each test measures.

item.title: Pool Maintenance Guide Index
item.description: All pool maintenance guides in one place — balancing sequence, tracking readings over time, seasonal and heat-wave adjustments.

item.title: Desert Pool Guide Index
item.description: All desert pool guides in one place — calcium creep, evaporation rates, when to drain, RO vs draining, Arizona-specific chemistry targets.

item.title: Reverse Osmosis vs. Draining a Pool: Which Is Right for Desert Pools?
item.description: RO removes dissolved minerals without losing water; draining replaces a fraction proportionally. In Arizona where fill water is already hard and water is scarce, choosing between the two matters more than most guides acknowledge.

item.title: When to Drain a Desert Pool: The 4 Signs It's Time
item.description: A partial drain-and-refill is annual maintenance for most desert pools — not an emergency. The four triggers are high CYA, high calcium hardness, very high TDS, and visible scale. Fall is the best time. A 25–33% drain typically resets both parameters for another season.

item.title: Why Arizona Pools Have High Calcium Hardness
item.description: Arizona tap water starts at 200–350 ppm calcium hardness — already at or above the recommended pool range. Combined with desert evaporation concentrating the pool all summer, calcium climbs without a single chemical addition. How to understand it, track it, and manage it.

item.title: Calcium Creep: Why Desert Pool Calcium Hardness Keeps Rising
item.description: Without adding a pound of calcium chloride, a desert pool gains 150–200 ppm calcium hardness over a summer. Evaporation concentrates every mineral; hard fill water adds more with every top-off. How the mechanism works, the math, and what to do when CH climbs too high.

item.title: Pool Chemistry During a Heat Wave: What to Watch and What to Do
item.description: Heat waves drain chlorine faster, raise LSI, and create ideal conditions for algae. Daily FC checks, higher FC targets, and watching LSI are your heat wave protocol.

item.title: Scale Inside a Salt Cell: How to Clean It and Prevent It
item.description: Calcium scale on salt cell plates cuts chlorine output and shortens cell life. Clean with diluted muriatic acid in 15–20 minutes — then fix your LSI so it stops coming back.

item.title: White Flakes from Pool Returns: 3 Causes and How to Fix Each
item.description: White flakes from pool returns are usually calcium scale breaking off your pipes or heater. Test calcium hardness and LSI — here's how to diagnose and fix each cause.

item.title: How CYA Changes Your LSI Calculation
item.description: Most LSI calculators use raw total alkalinity. The full formula subtracts CYA ÷ 3 before calculating the alkalinity factor. At 80 ppm CYA, the correction shifts LSI by around 0.15 — enough to move a pool from balanced to corrosive.

item.title: Why Your LSI Changes After It Rains
item.description: A heavy rainstorm can undo a week of careful chemistry work in a few hours. Rain dilutes calcium, alkalinity, and pH simultaneously — pushing LSI negative across all four inputs at once. Here's what happens to each factor and when to test after significant rain.

item.title: LSI by Pool Surface Type: Plaster, Vinyl, and Fiberglass
item.description: The LSI formula is the same for every pool. The consequences differ by surface. Corrosive water dissolves plaster directly, corrodes the metal walls behind vinyl liners, and leaves fiberglass gel coat intact but at risk from scale that is nearly impossible to remove without scratching.

item.title: CSI vs. LSI: Are They the Same Thing?
item.description: Pool apps and calculators use both CSI and LSI. Same formula structure, same target range — but the name doesn't tell you whether CYA correction or TDS is included. Here's what actually determines accuracy.

item.title: Desert Pool Chemistry: The Complete Guide for AZ & Southern California Pools
item.description: Desert pools face four problems national guides ignore: intense UV destroys chlorine faster, tap water is already very hard, evaporation concentrates minerals all season, and summer heat pushes water balance toward scale. The correct CYA targets, FC minimums, and calcium management for Arizona and Southern California pools.

item.title: Pool Evaporation in Hot Climates: Managing Water Loss and What It Does to Your Chemistry
item.description: Desert pools lose 1–1.5 inches of water per week in summer — and every gallon that evaporates leaves its mineral load behind, concentrating calcium, alkalinity, and CYA over the season. How to measure your pool's evaporation rate, reduce it with covers, and manage the chemistry consequences with a planned drain schedule.

item.title: Year-Round Pool Maintenance for Desert Pools
item.description: Arizona, Southern California, Nevada, and similar climates never close their pools — which means no annual chemistry reset and minerals that accumulate year over year. The season-by-season maintenance calendar for desert pool owners, including when to do a partial drain, how winter LSI flips toward corrosive, and the tracking advantage of year-round data.

item.title: Does High Alkalinity Cause Cloudy Pool Water?
item.description: When total alkalinity exceeds 120 ppm, it pushes pH up and forces calcium carbonate out of solution as a fine white haze. How to diagnose TA as the cloudiness cause, how to fix it with muriatic acid, and what to expect as the water clears.

item.title: Why Two LSI Calculators Can Give You Different Answers
item.description: Run the same pool readings through two LSI calculators and get different results. Here are the four formula differences — CYA correction, temperature method, TDS, and factor rounding — and which answer to trust.

item.title: LSI and Saltwater Pools: Why SWG Owners Need to Watch Water Balance More Closely
item.description: Every hour a salt chlorine generator runs, it pushes pH upward — making SWG pools uniquely prone to scale. How LSI explains the problem, why the salt cell is the most vulnerable component, and the right chemistry targets for SWG pools including TDS and CYA-corrected alkalinity.

item.title: Corrosive Pool Water: Causes, Warning Signs, and How to Fix It
item.description: Corrosive pool water etches plaster, dissolves grout, corrodes heater elements, and causes blue-green copper staining — even when pH looks fine. What causes it, how to spot it early, and how to fix it by raising LSI out of negative territory.

item.title: Pool Scale and Calcium Deposits: Causes, Prevention, and Removal
item.description: White crusty buildup on pool tile or salt cells is calcium carbonate scale — caused by oversaturated water. What causes it, how to remove calcium deposits from tile and equipment, and how to stop it from coming back by keeping LSI in range.

item.title: Pool Calcium Hardness: What It Is, Why It Matters, and How to Fix It
item.description: Low calcium hardness etches plaster and corrodes equipment. High calcium causes scale. Learn the target range for your pool type, how to raise calcium hardness with calcium chloride, and why no chemical can lower it — only a partial drain helps.

item.title: How to Track Pool Chemicals (A Simple System)
item.description: A simple 4-step system for tracking pool chemicals — test, record, dose, retest. What to log, what to skip, how often to log it, and how to pick the right tool (notebook, spreadsheet, or phone app).

item.title: Why You Should Track Pool Chemistry Over Time
item.description: A single pool test tells you today's water. Thirty tests tell you the pool itself — chlorine demand, pH drift triggers, CYA climb, equipment aging. The patterns you only see over time and why they matter.

item.title: Pool pH Keeps Rising? Here's Why (and How to Stop It)
item.description: Pool pH keeps coming back up no matter how much acid you add? The 6 root causes of stubborn pH drift — high alkalinity, salt cells, aeration, fresh plaster, and more — and how to fix the cause instead of the symptom.

item.title: Pool Alkalinity vs pH: What's the Difference?
item.description: pH is how acidic or basic your water is right now. Total alkalinity is the buffer that resists changes to pH. How they relate, how they affect each other, and which to fix first.

item.title: What Causes High Combined Chlorine in a Pool?
item.description: High combined chlorine comes from chloramines — chlorine that's reacted with sweat, urine, sunscreen, and organic debris. 6 main causes and how to fix it with breakpoint chlorination.

item.title: How Much Muriatic Acid to Add to a Pool (Dose Chart)
item.description: How much muriatic acid for your pool? Dose chart by pool size to lower pH 0.2–0.6 or alkalinity 10–30 ppm. Includes acid strengths, safety, and step-by-step.

item.title: Dead Algae but Pool Still Cloudy? Here's How to Clear It
item.description: Dead algae but pool still cloudy? Run the pump 24/7, clean the filter every 8–12 hours, add clarifier (or floc as last resort), and pass the OCLT before stopping.

item.title: Pool Turned Green Overnight? Emergency Triage Guide
item.description: Pool turned green overnight? It's a fresh algae bloom from chlorine dropping below your CYA minimum. Triage in 5 minutes, then hold FC at shock level to clear in 3–7 days.

item.title: What Is the Ideal Pool pH Level? (Target Ranges Explained)
item.description: The ideal pool pH is 7.4–7.8, with 7.5–7.6 the sweet spot. Learn why pH matters, target ranges, how to test, and how to adjust pH up or down safely.

item.title: How to Clear a Cloudy Pool Fast (24-Hour Plan)
item.description: Need to clear a cloudy pool fast? Follow this 5-step 24-hour plan: balance pH, shock to your CYA level, brush, clean the filter, and run the pump 24/7.

item.title: Why Won't Chlorine Stay in My Pool? 7 Causes & Fixes
item.description: Pool losing chlorine fast? The 7 most common causes — low CYA, high CYA, algae, organics, chloramines, underdosing, and heat — plus how to diagnose and fix each one.

item.title: Does Liquid Chlorine Raise CYA?
item.description: No — liquid chlorine (sodium hypochlorite) does not raise CYA. Only stabilized chlorine products like trichlor tablets and dichlor granules add cyanuric acid to your pool.

item.title: Why Is My Pool Cloudy After Shocking?
item.description: Pool still cloudy after shocking? It's usually dead algae, high pH, or not enough chlorine. Learn the 5 real causes and how to clear it up fast.

item.title: Best Time of Day to Test Pool Water
item.description: Morning before swimming gives the most accurate pool test results. Learn why timing matters for chlorine, pH, and alkalinity readings.

item.title: What Chemicals Do I Need for a Pool?
item.description: Every chemical a pool owner needs, what each one does, and which ones you can skip. A plain-language guide for new and experienced pool owners.

item.title: FC/CYA Chart: How Much Chlorine You Need
item.description: Free chlorine targets depend on your CYA level. Use this FC/CYA chart to find the right chlorine minimum for your pool and avoid algae problems.

item.title: Pool Startup Chemicals Checklist: Everything You Need
item.description: Complete checklist of chemicals you need to start up your pool — what each one does, how much to buy, and the order to add them.

item.title: How to Test Pool Water at Home: Step-by-Step Guide
item.description: Learn how to test your pool water at home — test strips vs liquid kits, which parameters to check, how to read results, and how often to test.

item.title: Baking Soda vs Soda Ash: Which One for Pools?
item.description: Baking soda raises alkalinity. Soda ash raises pH. Using the wrong one makes your pool chemistry worse. Learn which one you actually need and how much to add.

item.title: How to Raise Pool Chlorine Safely
item.description: Low free chlorine? Learn how to raise pool chlorine safely using liquid chlorine, cal-hypo, or tablets — with the right dose for your CYA level.

item.title: Pool Chlorine Too Low? Causes and How to Fix It
item.description: Pool chlorine too low? Learn why your FC keeps dropping, how CYA affects your minimum chlorine level, and how to raise it fast with the right dose.

item.title: Test Strips vs Liquid Test Kits: Which Is More Accurate?
item.description: Test strips are fast but liquid test kits are more accurate. Compare speed, precision, cost per test, and learn when to use each for pool water testing.

item.title: Opening Your Pool for Summer: Chemical Checklist
item.description: Step-by-step opening pool for summer checklist: physical prep, chemical order, exact targets, and common mistakes. Get your pool swim-ready in days, not weeks.

item.title: Pool Chemistry Cheat Sheet: Every Number You Need
item.description: The only pool chemistry cheat sheet you need. Every ideal range, every chemical dose, and every quick fix on one page. Bookmark this for poolside reference.

item.title: Pool pH Too High? Here's How to Fix It
item.description: Pool pH above 7.8? Learn why it happens, what damage it causes, and how to bring it down with muriatic acid — step by step.

item.title: Why Is My Pool Water Cloudy? (And How to Fix It)
item.description: Cloudy pool water has 5 common causes: low chlorine, high pH, high alkalinity, poor filtration, or high calcium. Here's how to diagnose and fix it.

item.title: Pool Water Green but Chlorine Is High? Here's Why
item.description: Green pool water despite high chlorine readings? The cause is usually high CYA, metals in the water, or a false chlorine reading. Here's how to diagnose and fix it.

item.title: Pool Chlorine Levels Chart: What Your Readings Mean
item.description: A clear chlorine levels chart for pool owners. Know what FC, TC, and CC readings mean, what ranges to aim for, and when to take action.

item.title: Liquid Chlorine vs Tablets: Pros and Cons
item.description: Liquid chlorine and tablets both sanitize your pool, but they affect your water chemistry differently. Compare cost, convenience, CYA impact, and when to use each.

item.title: How Often Should You Test Your Pool Water?
item.description: A realistic pool water testing schedule. Which chemicals to test weekly, monthly, and seasonally — and when to test more often.

item.title: How to Lower Pool Alkalinity (Without Wrecking Your pH)
item.description: High alkalinity makes pH impossible to control. Learn how to lower it with muriatic acid or dry acid — the right way, without crashing your pH.

item.title: Saltwater vs Chlorine Pools: Maintenance Comparison
item.description: Saltwater and chlorine pools both use chlorine — the difference is how it gets there. Compare costs, maintenance, chemistry, and which is right for you.

item.title: How to Balance Pool Water in 4 Steps
item.description: Balance your pool water in 4 steps: test, fix alkalinity first, then pH, then chlorine. Learn the correct order and why it matters.

item.title: Pool Chemistry for Beginners: The 5 Numbers That Matter
item.description: New pool owner? Learn the 5 essential numbers you need to track — free chlorine, pH, alkalinity, calcium hardness, and CYA — and what each one does.

item.title: Free Chlorine vs Total Chlorine: What's the Difference?
item.description: Free chlorine kills bacteria. Total chlorine includes the used-up part. Learn the difference, why combined chlorine matters, and what your readings actually mean.

item.title: Why LSI Matters for Your Pool — The Real Cost of Unbalanced Water
item.description: Corrosive pool water etches plaster and attacks metal fittings. Scale fouls heaters and salt cells. Here is what bad LSI actually costs — and how to catch it before the damage is visible.
